description:
Advances: ancora.gate

Why: the /ship-it critical review of ancora-gg8/field-friction (nine personas, consolidated report at ~/vaults/rmbrs-vault/code_review/critical/ancora/2026-09-05/ancora-gg8-field-friction/20260905-063249-consolidated.md) found one Critical and several reachable Highs. This ticket lands the must-fix subset on the branch before the PR opens. Base: e2fb6d2 (epic tip, contains releases 1.1.0 and 1.1.1). Read the consolidated report sections Consensus Findings and Fix Before Merge for the evidence behind each item; the individual reports are beside it.

Deliverable (each item names the defect, the file, and the proof):
1. CF1 (Critical) lib/ancora/gate.ex def_indexes/2: the Task.async_stream closure captures parsed_sources (the whole per-side AST map), so every worker copies the whole map. Hoist the lookup: map each {path, modules} to {path, modules, Map.fetch(parsed_sources, path)} before the stream and match on the fetched value inside. Proof: a test that traces or measures that a worker never receives the full map is hard; instead add a test asserting def_indexes still builds the same indexes and keep the determinism and parse-count tests green, and record before/after wall time on the synthetic corpus the performance reviewer left at the scratchpad proj directory (if present) in the IMPLEMENTED record.
2. CF4 (High) lib/ancora/review.ex drift_cards/2 filters on the literal "derived/drift", so derived/drift_transitive gets no card and acknowledged_cards/5 stamps it :acknowledged (green). Give transitive drift its own card and badge (:drift_transitive, styled as info, not as pass), and make acknowledged_cards/5 claim only findings whose severity_source is :ack. Update .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md (badge statement) in the same diff. Tests: a review fixture with one transitive drift finding renders the new badge and never the acknowledged badge; an acknowledged finding still renders acknowledged.
3. CF5 (High) lib/ancora/gate.ex hidden_by_source buckets default/trailer/ack and omits :config, which is what Finding.source returns for a config.yml severities or overrides demotion (lib/ancora/severity.ex). Add the config bucket everywhere the three appear: the rollup, the branch summary line grammar in Output, --explain-acks (include config-demoted findings), the JSON report, and the statement in .spec/specs/ancora.findings.spec.md that enumerates the sources. Tests: a fixture with one config-demoted info finding shows hidden config=1 on the real Output path and in the spec.check subprocess golden; existing goldens gain the config=0 column.
4. F18 (High) lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex governs?/3 accepts a governing ADR at any status; the append guards (lib/ancora/append_only.ex) require status accepted and the scenario under the requirement already says accepted. Require accepted in governs?/3; add the word to the requirement text if missing and a scenario plus test where a proposed or superseded ADR does not clear change/missing_decision.
5. CF3 (Medium, crash) lib/ancora/index.ex task_value!/1 and lib/ancora/tag_scanner.ex call exit(reason) on an {:exit, _} stream element, and those {:exit, _} clauses in all four parallel loops are unreachable anyway because the caller does not trap exits, so a raise inside a worker (File.read! on a spec path removed mid-run) kills the mix task with a raw EXIT and no verdict line. Make each worker function catch its own failures and return {:error, reason} (wrap the body in try/rescue producing a tagged tuple), remove the exit() calls, keep or drop the {:exit, _} clauses consistently, and give the new error atoms (parsed_source_missing, def_index_exit, source_scan_exit, and the new worker-failure tuple) gate_error/1 clauses that return {:env, message} instead of falling into the catch-all raise at lib/ancora/gate.ex ~550. Tests: a fixture whose spec file is a directory (File.read! raises) yields an :env-tier error with a verdict line, on the real Gate.check path; one unit test per new gate_error clause.
6. CF7 and CF6 (High/Medium) lib/ancora/output.ex json_safe/1 hand-lists six keys and drops the new requirement field; lib/ancora/finding.ex renders four messages as "#{subject}.#{requirement}" although the requirement id passed is already fully qualified, producing "ancora.derive.ancora.derive.x" (append/statement_changed, tags/requirement_untagged, tags/new_requirement_untagged, spec/requirement_unverified). Add requirement to the JSON shape (document it in the JSON contract statement in ancora.tasks or ancora.findings spec as an optional field) and print the id bare in the four renderers. Tests: JSON report includes requirement for a tag_borrowed finding; message assertions for the four codes contain the id exactly once.
7. CF11 (Medium) lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex builds tags/tag_borrowed with no subject, so no overrides: entry can ever match it. Set subject: from the requirement id owner (the index knows which subject defines the requirement). Test: a config override for tags/tag_borrowed on that subject changes its severity.
8. F23 (Medium) lib/ancora/gate.ex guidance next= is a hardcoded string; when findings are hidden it should name --verbose and --explain-acks. Derive it from the report: if hidden counts are all zero keep the current text; otherwise say how many are hidden and which flag shows them. Test on the real Output path.
9. Docs (Medium): surface: is undocumented. Add a short section to docs/migration.md and README.md (what it is, exact repo-relative paths, what happens to bindings outside it, that an empty list is not yet defined and should not be used) and mention it in priv/spec_init/agents/SKILL.md.eex; restore a subject-only override example in priv/spec_init/config.yml next to the requirement-scoped one. docs_test assertions as needed.
10. Test fix: test/ancora/gate_test.exs sync_traces/2 calls :erlang.trace_delivered(self()) while the traced work runs in async_stream children; use :erlang.trace_delivered(:all).

Verification:
- Tests to pass: full mix test; mix compile --warnings-as-errors; mix format --check-formatted; mix deps.unlock --check-unused; mix spec.check --base origin/main (result=pass; new spec statements carry the decisions: link to ancora.decision.field_friction_response; transitive drift may use the standing one-trailer ruling, Spec-Ack: derived/drift=info with a body line naming the transitive subjects).
- Behaviors to demonstrate: items 1-8 each have the named test; the determinism, parse-count and ordering tests stay green; goldens updated only for the config=0 column.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: targeted test files plus mix spec.validate.
  - Final tier: before IMPLEMENTED, full mix test plus mix spec.check --base origin/main, run-until-green, 2-run cap.
  - Verifier tier: cold; mix spec.check --base origin/main and targeted files; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks: every new clause has a test that fails when the clause is removed; production call site named for each new callable; spec surfaces fresh for every touched callable.

Allowed touches (this stage may modify): lib/ancora/gate.ex, lib/ancora/review.ex, lib/ancora/output.ex, lib/ancora/finding.ex, lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex, lib/ancora/index.ex, lib/ancora/tag_scanner.ex, lib/ancora/derive/module_locator.ex (exit clause consistency only), lib/ancora/severity.ex (only if the source enumeration needs it), .spec/specs/ancora.review.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.findings.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.tasks.spec.md, .spec/specs/ancora.parsing.spec.md, docs/migration.md, README.md, .spec/README.md, priv/spec_init/agents/SKILL.md.eex, priv/spec_init/config.yml, priv/review/** (badge style), test/**.

Out of Scope (intent): the nine TRACK items in the consolidated report (override precedence, surface: [] semantics, off counting, explain-acks add-vs-replace, tag rename semantics, memo statement wording, AST retention redesign, status partial label, the scale bench) are design decisions and go to the fast-follow epic; do not touch them. No refactors beyond the items above (no helper consolidation, no SourceScan rewrite, no Config.restrict).

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Full suite passes
- [ ] mix spec.check --base origin/main passes
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Cold verifier PASS comment on the ticket
title: Critical-review fixes before the field-friction PR
